name: Mistral: Ministral 3 3B 2512
description:
Here is how to read the Mistral: Ministral 3 3B 2512 config.json. The architecture class is Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 3,072: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 131,072 × 3,072: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 32, so each head sees 128 dimensions (3,072 / 32). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 3072 / 32 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_key_value_heads is 8, so this is grouped-query attention (GQA): 32 query heads share 8 key/value groups, so the KV cache is about 4× smaller than full MHA.

num_hidden_layers is 26: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 9,216. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 3,072-wide stream is projected up, activated with silu, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 262,144 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is.

vocab_size is 131,072. 131,072 is divisible by 256, the usual vocab-tiling grain. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

tie_word_embeddings is true: the same matrix is reused for input embeddings and the LM head.

torch_dtype is bfloat16. Brain floating point keeps FP32’s exponent range with less mantissa, which avoids the overflow/underflow of a tiny exponent at the cost of noisier decimals — and it halves the on-chip footprint versus FP32. NVIDIA A100s were the first NVIDIA chips with native BF16; Huawei Ascend 910-class parts also prefer BF16/FP16 on the cube.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Reasoning-2512/blob/main/config.json.
